evals.query: I just realized I used @Autowired in a Kora service instead of constructor injection and had to fix it. Record this.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py add with a title and --context, --problem, --solution, --files arguments
Frames the entry as Kora incorrect usage (Spring @Autowired instead of Kora constructor injection)
Stores the entry as a separate Markdown file under ~/.kora-journal/<project>/<module>/<YYYY-MM-DD>_slug.md
Does not hand-write the journal file when the CLI is available and does not invent extra add subcommand flags

evals.query: Add a journal entry: our checkout total was computing tax before the discount, I fixed the business rule order.
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is application business logic, not Kora Framework incorrect usage, and is out of scope for the journal
Declines to add the entry and explains the journal records only Kora misuse (wrong annotation, hallucinated API, misapplied pattern)
Does not run kora_journal.py add for this domain/business change

evals.query: Before I implement an HTTP client interceptor for auth in Kora, check the journal for prior issues.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py search with the relevant keywords (e.g. "http interceptor auth") and a --limit
Optionally uses --by-tags for a tag-only search or --status to filter
Reads the matched entry file and applies the recorded solution
Does not skip the search or invent a query subcommand that the CLI does not provide

evals.query: I applied the fix from a pending journal entry into the skill docs. Mark it done.
expected_behavior: Runs kora_journal.py integrate <entry-file> to mark the entry integrated
Explains pending -> integrated status transition after the fix is folded into the skills
Does not delete the entry or edit its status field by hand when the CLI subcommand exists
